scope: The whitewashed Larabanga Mosque after restoration, around the 2010 Qualla publication. The exterior includes the tapered earthen buttresses, projecting timber torons, tall minaret and mihrab tower, and the small entrance with its patterned panel.

originalReview.notes: The frontal photograph shows the white walls, dark plinth, thick buttresses, protruding timber, triangular grille and two unequal towers. The native upload date anchors the representation.
The March 2006 post-restoration view shows the projecting buttresses, earth-plaster forms and timber from the baobab side. Haruna Mohammed’s image controls the modeled white finish.

quallaSearch.notes: The two exact published Qualla originals match their native first-party public-domain releases. The frontal image publication in 2010 is the era anchor. The 2006 view supports the adjoining side after the same restoration. No supplemental imagery was used.
